verses.text: Moreover di Spirit lift me up, and bring me to di east gate of di Lord house, wey face eastward. See, for di entrance of di gate dey 25 men. Among dem I see Jaazaniah, Azzur pikin, and Pelatiah, Benaiah pikin, princes of di people.
Den e talk to me, “Son of man, dis na di men wey devise iniquity, and give wicked counsel for dis city,
wey talk, ‘Di time no near to build houses. Dis city na di cooking pot, and we be di meat.’
Therefore prophesy against dem. Prophesy, son of man.”
Di Spirit of di Lord fall on me, and e talk to me, “Speak, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: Dis na wetin una don talk, house of Israel, because I know di things wey come into una mind.
Una don multiply una slain for dis city, and don fill di streets of am with di slain.’
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Una slain wey una don lay for di middle of am, dem na di meat, and dis city na di cooking pot, but I go bring una out of di middle of am.
Una don fear di sword, and I go bring sword on una,’ talk di Lord God.
‘I go bring una out of di middle of am, and deliver una into di hand of strangers, and execute judgments among una.
Una go fall by di sword. I go judge una for di border of Israel. Una go know say I be di Lord.
Dis city no go be una cooking pot, neither una go be di meat for di middle of am. I go judge una for di border of Israel.
Una go know say I be di Lord, because una no waka for my statutes, neither execute my ordinances, but don do according to di ordinances of di nations wey dey round about una.’”
E happen, when I prophesy, say Pelatiah, Benaiah pikin, die. Den I fall down on my face, and cry with loud voice, and talk, “Ah Lord God! You go make full end of di remnant of Israel?”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Son of man, your brothers, even your brothers, di men of your kindred, and all di house of Israel, all of dem, na dem di inhabitants of Jerusalem don talk to, ‘Go far from di Lord. Dis land dey given to us for possession.’

Therefore talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Although I don cast dem far off among di nations, and although I don scatter dem among di countries, yet I go be to dem as sanctuary for little while for di countries where dem don come.’
Therefore talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: I go gather una from di peoples, and assemble una out of di countries where una don dey scattered, and I go give una di land of Israel.’
Dem go come dere, and dem go take away all di detestable things and all di abominations of am from dere.
I go give dem one heart, and I go put new spirit inside dem. I go take di stony heart out of dem flesh, and go give dem heart of flesh,
so that dem go waka for my statutes, and keep my ordinances, and do dem. Dem go be my people, and I go be dem God.
But as for dem whose heart waka after di heart of dem detestable things and dem abominations, I go bring dem way on dem own heads,” talk di Lord God.
Den di cherubim lift up dem wings, and di wheels beside dem. Di glory of di God of Israel dey over dem above.
Di glory of di Lord go up from di middle of di city, and stand on di mountain wey dey di east side of di city.
Di Spirit lift me up, and bring me in di vision by di Spirit of God into Chaldea, to dem of di captivity. So di vision wey I don see go up from me.
Den I speak to dem of di captivity all di things wey di Lord don show me.
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, you dwell for di middle of rebellious house, wey get eyes to see, and no see, wey get ears to hear, and no hear, because dem na rebellious house.

Therefore, you son of man, prepare for yourself baggage for moving, and move by day for dem sight. You go move from your place to another place for dem sight. Maybe dem go consider, though dem na rebellious house.
You go bring out your baggage by day for dem sight, as baggage for moving. You go go out yourself at evening for dem sight, as when dem go out into exile.
Dig for yourself through di wall for dem sight, and carry out through am.
For dem sight you go carry am on your shoulder, and carry am out for di dark. You go cover your face, so that you no see di ground, because I don set you for sign to di house of Israel.”

I do so as I dey commanded. I bring out my baggage by day, as baggage for moving, and for evening I dig through di wall with my hand. I bring am out for di dark, and carry am on my shoulder for dem sight.
For di morning di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, di house of Israel, di rebellious house, no talk to you, ‘Wetin you dey do?’
Talk to dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Dis burden concern di prince for Jerusalem, and all di house of Israel wey dey among dem.’
Talk, ‘I be your sign. Like how I don do, so e go dey done to dem. Dem go go into exile, into captivity.
Di prince wey dey among dem go carry on im shoulder for di dark, and go go out. Dem go dig through di wall to carry out through am. E go cover im face, so that e no go see di ground with im eyes.
I go spread my net on am, and e go dey taken for my snare. I go bring am to Babylon, to di land of di Chaldeans, yet e no go see am, though e go die dere.
I go scatter toward every wind all wey dey round about am to help am, and all im troops. I go draw out sword after dem.
Dem go know say I be di Lord, when I don scatter dem among di nations, and disperse dem through di countries.
But I go leave few men of dem from di sword, from di famine, and from di pestilence, so that dem go declare all dem abominations among di nations where dem go. Dem go know say I be di Lord.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with fearfulness.

Talk to di people of di land, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis concerning di inhabitants of Jerusalem, and di land of Israel: Dem go eat dem bread with fearfulness, and drink dem water with dismay, so that di land go dey desolate from all wey dey inside am, because of di violence of all wey dwell inside am.
Di cities wey dey inhabited go dey laid waste, and di land go be desolation. Una go know say I be di Lord.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, wetin be dis proverb wey una get for di land of Israel, saying, ‘Di days dey prolonged, and every vision fail’?

Tell dem therefore, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: I go make dis proverb cease, and dem no go use am as proverb in Israel any more.’ But talk to dem, ‘Di days dey near, and di fulfilment of every vision.
Because no more false vision or flattering divination go dey within di house of Israel.

Because I be di Lord. I go speak, and di word wey I go speak go come to pass. E no go dey prolonged any more. Because for una days, rebellious house, I go speak di word, and go perform am,’ talk di Lord God.”
Again di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, see, di house of Israel talk, ‘Di vision wey e see na for many days to come, and e dey prophesy of times wey dey far off.’
Therefore tell dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: None of my words go dey prolonged any more, but di word wey I speak go dey performed,’ talk di Lord God.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, prophesy against di prophets of Israel wey prophesy, and talk to dem wey prophesy out of dem own heart, ‘Hear di word of di Lord.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: Woe to di foolish prophets, wey follow dem own spirit, and don see nothing!
Israel, your prophets don be like foxes for di waste places.
You no go up into di gaps, neither build up di wall for di house of Israel, to stand for di battle for di day of di Lord.
Dem don see vanity and lying divination, wey talk, ‘Di Lord talk,’ but di Lord no send dem. Dem don make people hope say di word go dey confirmed.
No be say una don see vain vision, and don speak lying divination, whereas una talk, ‘Di Lord talk,’ but I no speak?
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: Because una don speak vanity, and see lies, therefore see, I dey against una,” talk di Lord God.

“My hand go dey against di prophets wey see vanity, and wey divine lies. Dem no go dey for di council of my people, neither dem go dey written for di writing of di house of Israel, neither dem go enter into di land of Israel. Una go know say I be di Lord God.
Because, even because dem don lead my people astray, saying, ‘Peace,’ and no peace dey. When one build wall, see, dem plaster am with whitewash.
Talk to dem wey plaster am with whitewash say e go fall. Flooding rain go come, and I go send great hailstones to fall, and stormy wind go tear am.
See, when di wall don fall, e no go dey said to una, ‘Where di plaster wey una plaster am with dey?’
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: I go even tear am with stormy wind for my wrath. Flooding rain go dey for my anger, and great hailstones for consuming wrath.

So I go break down di wall wey una don plaster with whitewash, and bring am down to di ground, so that im foundation go dey uncovered. E go fall, and una go dey consumed inside am. Una go know say I be di Lord.
Thus I go accomplish my wrath on di wall, and on dem wey don plaster am with whitewash. I go talk to una, ‘Di wall no dey again, nor dem wey plaster am,
I mean di prophets of Israel wey prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and wey see vision of peace for am, and no peace dey,’ talk di Lord God.”
“You, son of man, set your face against di daughters of your people, wey prophesy out of dem own heart, and prophesy against dem,

and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Woe to di women wey sew magic bands upon all elbows, and make veils for di heads of persons of every stature to hunt souls! Una go hunt di souls of my people, and keep souls alive for una own gain?

Una don profane me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to kill di souls wey no suppose die, and to keep alive di souls wey no suppose live, by una lying to my people wey listen to lies.

Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: See, I dey against una magic bands, wey una dey hunt di souls with like birds, and I go tear dem from una arms. I go let di souls go, even di souls wey una hunt like birds.
I go also tear una veils, and deliver my people out of una hand, and dem no go dey in una hand to be hunted any more. Una go know say I be di Lord.
Because with lies una don make di heart of di righteous sad, wey I no make sad, and strengthen di hands of di wicked, so that e no go return from im wicked way, by promising am life.
Therefore una no go see vanity, nor divine divinations any more. I go deliver my people out of una hand. Una go know say I be di Lord.’”
Some of di elders of Israel come to me, and sit before me.
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, dis men don set up dem idols for dem heart, and put di stumbling block of dem iniquity before dem face. I go dey inquired of at all by dem?

Therefore speak to dem, and talk to dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Every man of di house of Israel wey set up im idols for im heart, and put di stumbling block of im iniquity before im face, and come to di prophet, I di Lord go answer am wey come according to di multitude of im idols,
so that I go take di house of Israel for dem own heart, because dem don all dey estranged from me through dem idols.’
Therefore talk to di house of Israel, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Return, and turn una from una idols, and turn away una faces from all una abominations.

Because everyone of di house of Israel, or of di strangers wey sojourn for Israel, wey separate imself from me, and set up im idols for im heart, and put di stumbling block of im iniquity before im face, and come to di prophet to inquire for imself of me, I di Lord go answer am by myself.
I go set my face against dat man, and go make am sign and proverb, and I go cut am off from di middle of my people. Una go know say I be di Lord.
If di prophet dey deceived and speak word, I di Lord don deceive dat prophet, and I go stretch out my hand on am, and go destroy am from di middle of my people Israel.
Dem go bear dem iniquity. Di iniquity of di prophet go be even as di iniquity of am wey seek am,
so that di house of Israel no go go astray from me any more, neither dey polluted any more with all dem transgressions, but dem go be my people, and I go be dem God,’ talk di Lord God.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, when land sin against me by committing trespass, and I stretch out my hand on am, and break di staff of bread for am, and send famine on am, and cut off from am man and animal,
though dis three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, dey inside am, dem go deliver only dem own souls by dem righteousness,” talk di Lord God.
“If I cause evil animals to pass through di land, and dem ravage am, and e dey desolate, so that no man fit pass through because of di animals,
though dis three men dey inside am, as I live,” talk di Lord God, “dem go deliver neither sons nor daughters. Dem only go dey delivered, but di land go dey desolate.”
“Or if I bring sword on dat land, and talk, ‘Sword, go through di land,’ so that I cut off from am man and animal,
though dis three men dey inside am, as I live,” talk di Lord God, “dem go deliver neither sons nor daughters, but dem only go dey delivered demselves.”
“Or if I send pestilence into dat land, and pour out my wrath on am in blood, to cut off from am man and animal,
though Noah, Daniel, and Job dey inside am, as I live,” talk di Lord God, “dem go deliver neither son nor daughter. Dem go deliver only dem own souls by dem righteousness.”
For di Lord God talk like dis: “How much more when I send my four severe judgments on Jerusalem, di sword, and di famine, and di evil animals, and di pestilence, to cut off from am man and animal?

Yet see, dem go leave remnant inside am, wey go dey carried out, both sons and daughters. See, dem go come out to una, and una go see dem way and dem doings. Una go dey comforted concerning di evil wey I don bring on Jerusalem, even concerning all wey I don bring on am.
Dem go comfort una, when una see dem way and dem doings. Una go know say I no don do without cause all wey I don do inside am,” talk di Lord God.
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, wetin di vine tree be more pass any tree, di vine branch wey dey among di trees of di forest?
Wood go dey taken from am to make anything? Or men go take peg from am to hang any vessel on am?
See, e dey given to di fire for fuel. Di fire don devour both ends of am, and di middle of am don burn. E go dey profitable for any work?
See, when e dey whole, e no dey fit for any work. How much less, when di fire don devour am, and e don burn, e go still dey fit for any work?”
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: “As di vine tree among di trees of di forest, wey I don give to di fire for fuel, so I go give di inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I go set my face against dem. Dem go go out from di fire, but di fire go still devour dem. Una go know say I be di Lord, when I set my face against dem.
I go make di land desolate, because dem don commit trespass,” talk di Lord God.
Again di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know im abominations,
and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth na of di land of di Canaanite. Your father na di Amorite, and your mother na Hittite.
As for your birth, for di day wey you dey born, dem no cut your navel string, neither dem wash you with water to cleanse you. You no dey salted at all, nor wrapped in cloths.
No eye pity you, to do any of dis things to you, to have compassion on you, but you dey cast out for di open field, because of di loathing of your life, for di day wey you dey born.
When I pass by you, and see you wallowing for your blood, I talk to you, “Live!” Yes, I talk to you wey dey in your blood, “Live!”
I cause you to multiply like di plant of di field, and you increase and grow great, and you come to excellent beauty. Your breasts dey formed, and your hair dey grown, yet you dey naked and bare.

Now when I pass by you, and look at you, see, your time na di time of love, and I spread my skirt over you, and cover your nakedness. Yes, I swear to you, and enter into covenant with you,’ talk di Lord God, ‘and you become mine.
Den I wash you with water. Yes, I thoroughly wash away your blood from you, and I anoint you with oil.
I clothe you also with embroidered work, and put leather sandals on you. I wrap you with fine linen, and cover you with silk.
I decorate you with ornaments, and put bracelets on your hands, and chain on your neck.
I put ring on your nose, and earrings in your ears, and beautiful crown on your head.

Thus you dey decorated with gold and silver. Your clothing na fine linen, and silk, and embroidered work. You eat fine flour, and honey, and oil. You dey exceedingly beautiful, and you prosper to royal estate.
Your renown go out among di nations for your beauty, because e dey perfect through my majesty wey I put on you,’ talk di Lord God.
‘But you trust for your beauty, and play di prostitute because of your renown, and pour out your prostitution on everyone wey pass by. E be im own.
You take some of your garments, and make for yourself high places decorated with various colours, and play di prostitute for dem. Such things no suppose happen, neither go happen.
You take also your beautiful jewels of my gold and of my silver, wey I give you, and make for yourself images of men, and play di prostitute with dem.
You take your embroidered garments, and cover dem, and set my oil and my incense before dem.
My bread also wey I give you, di fine flour, and oil, and honey, wey I feed you with, you even set am before dem for sweet savour, and so e be,’ talk di Lord God.
‘Moreover you take your sons and your daughters, wey you don bear to me, and dem you sacrifice to dem to dey devoured. Dis your prostitution na small matter,
say you don kill my children, and deliver dem up, in causing dem to pass through di fire to dem?
For all your abominations and your prostitution you no remember di days of your youth, when you dey naked and bare, and dey wallowing for your blood.
E happen after all your wickedness (woe, woe to you!),’ talk di Lord God,
‘say you don build for yourself vaulted place, and don make for yourself lofty place for every street.
You don build your lofty place at every head of di way, and don make your beauty abominable, and don open your feet to everyone wey pass by, and multiply your prostitution.
You don also play di prostitute with di Egyptians, your neighbours, great of flesh, and don multiply your prostitution, to provoke me to anger.
See, therefore, I don stretch out my hand over you, and don diminish your portion, and deliver you to di will of dem wey hate you, di daughters of di Philistines, wey dey ashamed of your lewd way.
You don play di prostitute also with di Assyrians, because you dey insatiable. Yes, you don play di prostitute with dem, and yet you no dey satisfied.
You don also multiply your prostitution to di land of merchants, to Chaldea. Yet even dis no satisfy you.
How your heart dey weak,’ talk di Lord God, ‘seeing say you do all dis things, di work of imperious prostitute,
in that you build your vaulted place for di head of every way, and make your lofty place for every street, and no be like prostitute, because you scorn payment.
Adulterous wife, wey take strangers instead of her husband!
Dem give gifts to all prostitutes, but you give your gifts to all your lovers, and bribe dem, so that dem go come to you on every side for your prostitution.
Di contrary dey for you from other women for your prostitution, because none dey wey follow you to play di prostitute. In that you give payment, and no payment dey given to you, so you dey contrary.’
Therefore, prostitute, hear di word of di Lord.

Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Because your filthiness dey poured out, and your nakedness uncovered through your prostitution with your lovers, and with all di idols of your abominations, and because of di blood of your children, wey you give to dem,

therefore see, I go gather all your lovers, wey you don take pleasure with, and all wey you don love, with all wey you don hate. I go even gather dem against you from every side, and go uncover your nakedness to dem, so that dem go see all your nakedness.
I go judge you as women wey break wedlock and shed blood dey judged, and I go bring blood on you for fury and jealousy.

I go also give you into dem hand, and dem go throw down your vaulted place, and break down your lofty places. Dem go strip you of your clothes, and take your beautiful jewels, and leave you naked and bare.
Dem go also bring up assembly against you, and dem go stone you with stones, and thrust you through with dem swords.
Dem go burn your houses with fire, and execute judgments on you for di sight of many women. I go cause you to cease from playing di prostitute, and you no go give payment any more.
So I go cause my wrath toward you to rest, and my jealousy go depart from you, and I go dey quiet, and no go dey angry any more.

Because you no remember di days of your youth, but don provoke me with all dis things, see, therefore I also go bring your way on your head,’ talk di Lord God. ‘You no go commit lewdness above all your abominations.
See, everyone wey use proverbs go use dis proverb against you, saying, “As di mother, so im daughter.”
You na your mother daughter, wey loathe her husband and her children. You na di sister of your sisters, wey loathe dem husbands and dem children. Your mother na Hittite, and your father na Amorite.
Your elder sister na Samaria, wey dwell at your left hand, she and her daughters. Your younger sister, wey dwell at your right hand, na Sodom and her daughters.
Yet you no waka for dem ways, nor do after dem abominations. But, as if dat na very little thing, you dey more corrupt pass dem for all your ways.
As I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘Sodom your sister no do, she nor her daughters, as you don do, you and your daughters.
See, dis na di iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and prosperous ease dey for her and for her daughters. She no strengthen di hand of di poor and needy.
Dem dey haughty, and commit abomination before me. Therefore I take dem away as I see good.
Samaria no commit half of your sins, but you don multiply your abominations more pass dem, and don justify your sisters by all your abominations wey you don do.

You also, bear your own disgrace, in that you don give judgment for your sisters. Through your sins wey you don commit more abominable pass dem, dem dey more righteous pass you. Yes, dey ashamed also, and bear your disgrace, in that you don justify your sisters.
I go cause dem captivity to return, di captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and di captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and di captivity of your captives among dem,
so that you go bear your own disgrace, and go dey ashamed for all wey you don do, in that you dey comfort to dem.
Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, go return to dem former estate. Samaria and her daughters go return to dem former estate. You and your daughters go return to your former estate.
Sodom your sister no dey mentioned by your mouth for di day of your pride,
before your wickedness dey uncovered, as for di time of di reproach of di daughters of Syria, and of all wey dey round about her, di daughters of di Philistines, wey despise you all round.
You don bear your lewdness and your abominations,’ talk di Lord.
For di Lord God talk like dis: ‘I go also deal with you as you don do, wey don despise di oath by breaking di covenant.
Nevertheless I go remember my covenant with you for di days of your youth, and I go establish for you everlasting covenant.
Den you go remember your ways, and dey ashamed, when you receive your sisters, your elder and your younger. I go give dem to you for daughters, but no by your covenant.
I go establish my covenant with you. Den you go know say I be di Lord,
so that you go remember, and dey confounded, and no open your mouth any more because of your shame, when I don forgive you all wey you don do,’ talk di Lord God.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, put forth riddle, and speak parable to di house of Israel,
and talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: Great eagle wey get great wings and long feathers, full of feathers wey get various colours, come to Lebanon, and take di top of di cedar.
E crop off di topmost of im young twigs, and carry am to land of merchants. E set am for city of traders.
E take also of di seed of di land, and plant am for fruitful soil. E place am beside many waters. E set am as willow tree.
E grow, and become spreading vine of low stature, wey im branches turn toward am, and im roots dey under am. So e become vine, and bring forth branches, and shoot forth sprigs.

Another great eagle dey also wey get great wings and many feathers. See, dis vine bend im roots toward am, and shoot forth im branches toward am, from di beds where e dey planted, so that e go water am.
E dey planted for good soil by many waters, so that e go bring forth branches, and bear fruit, so that e go be good vine.’

Talk, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis: E go prosper? E no go pull up im roots, and cut off im fruit, so that e go wither? All im fresh sprouting leaves go wither. E no go need great power or many people to pluck am up by di roots.
Yes, see, e dey planted. E go prosper? E no go wither utterly, when di east wind touch am? E go wither for di beds where e grow.’”
Moreover di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Say now to di rebellious house, ‘Una no know wetin dis things mean?’ Tell dem, ‘See, di king of Babylon come to Jerusalem, and take di king of am, and di princes of am, and lead dem with am to Babylon.
E take of di royal offspring, and make covenant with am. E bring am under oath, and take away di mighty of di land,
so that di kingdom go be brought low, that e no go lift imself up, but that by keeping im covenant e go stand.
But e rebel against am by sending im ambassadors to Egypt, so that dem go give am horses and many people. E go prosper? E go escape wey do such things? E go break covenant, and still escape?
As I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘surely for di place where di king dwell wey make am king, whose oath e despise, and whose covenant e break, even with am for di middle of Babylon e go die.
Pharaoh with im mighty army and great company no go help am for di war, when dem cast up mounds and build siege walls to cut off many persons.
Because e despise di oath by breaking di covenant, and see, e don give im hand, yet e don do all dis things. E no go escape.’
Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: ‘As I live, surely my oath wey e despise, and my covenant wey e break, I go bring am on im own head.
I go spread my net on am, and e go dey taken for my snare. I go bring am to Babylon, and go enter into judgment with am dere for im trespass wey e don trespass against me.
All im fugitives, with all im troops, go fall by di sword, and dem wey remain go dey scattered toward every wind. Una go know say I, di Lord, don speak am.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘I myself go take of di lofty top of di cedar, and go plant am. I go crop off from di topmost of im young twigs tender one, and I go plant am on high and lofty mountain.

On di mountain of di height of Israel I go plant am. E go bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be goodly cedar. Under am go dwell all birds of every wing. For di shadow of im branches dem go dwell.

All di trees of di field go know say I, di Lord, don bring down di high tree, don exalt di low tree, don dry up di green tree, and don make di dry tree flourish. I, di Lord, don speak am and don do am.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Wetin una mean say una dey use dis proverb concerning di land of Israel, saying, ‘Di fathers don eat sour grapes, and di teeth of di children dey set on edge’?
As I live,” talk di Lord God, “una go no more get occasion to use dis proverb for Israel.
See, all souls na mine. As di soul of di father, so also di soul of di son na mine. Di soul wey sin, e go die.
But if man dey just, and do wetin dey lawful and right,
and no eat on di mountains, neither lift up im eyes to di idols of di house of Israel, neither defile im neighbour wife, neither come near to woman for her uncleanness,
and no wrong any, but restore to di debtor im pledge, commit no robbery, give im bread to di hungry, and cover di naked with clothing,
e no lend at interest, neither take any increase, but withdraw im hand from iniquity, and execute true justice between man and man,
e waka for my statutes, and keep my ordinances, to deal truly. Dat na just man. E go surely live,” talk di Lord God.
“If e beget son wey be robber, shedder of blood, wey do any one of dis things,
and wey no do any of dose duties, but even eat on di mountains, and defile im neighbour wife,
wey wrong di poor and needy, commit robbery, no restore di pledge, and lift up im eyes to di idols, commit abomination,
e lend at interest, and take increase. Dat one go live? E no go live. E don do all dis abominations. E go surely die. Im blood go dey on am.
Now see, if e beget son wey see all im father sins wey e do, and fear, and no do such like,
e no eat on di mountains, neither lift up im eyes to di idols of di house of Israel, neither defile im neighbour wife,
neither wrong any, neither take pledge, neither commit robbery, but give im bread to di hungry, and cover di naked with clothing,
e withdraw im hand from di poor, e no receive interest nor increase, e execute my ordinances, and waka for my statutes, e no go die for di iniquity of im father. E go surely live.
As for im father, because e cruelly oppress, rob im brother, and do wetin no good among im people, see, e go die for im iniquity.
Yet una talk, ‘Why di son no bear di iniquity of di father?’ When di son don do wetin dey lawful and right, and don keep all my statutes, and don do dem, e go surely live.

Di soul wey sin, e go die. Di son no go bear di iniquity of di father, neither di father go bear di iniquity of di son. Di righteousness of di righteous go dey on am, and di wickedness of di wicked go dey on am.
But if di wicked turn from all im sins wey e don commit, and keep all my statutes, and do wetin dey lawful and right, e go surely live. E no go die.
None of im transgressions wey e don commit go dey remembered against am. For im righteousness wey e don do e go live.
I get any pleasure at all say di wicked go die?” talk di Lord God, “and no say e go return from im ways, and live?

But when di righteous turn away from im righteousness, and commit iniquity, and do according to all di abominations wey di wicked man do, e go live? None of im righteous deeds wey e don do go dey remembered. For im trespass wey e don trespass, and for im sin wey e don sin, for dem e go die.
Yet una talk, ‘Di way of di Lord no dey equal.’ Hear now, house of Israel: My way no dey equal? Una ways no dey unequal?
When di righteous man turn away from im righteousness, and commit iniquity, and die inside am, e go die for im iniquity wey e don do.
Again, when di wicked man turn away from im wickedness wey e don commit, and do wetin dey lawful and right, e go save im soul alive.
Because e consider, and turn away from all im transgressions wey e don commit, e go surely live. E no go die.
Yet di house of Israel talk, ‘Di way of di Lord no dey equal.’ House of Israel, my ways no dey equal? Una ways no dey unequal?
Therefore I go judge una, house of Israel, everyone according to im ways,” talk di Lord God. “Repent, and turn from all una transgressions, so that iniquity no go be una ruin.
Cast away from una all una transgressions wey una don transgress, and make una new heart and new spirit. Because why una go die, house of Israel?
Because I no get pleasure for di death of am wey die,” talk di Lord God. “So turn una, and live.”
“Moreover, take up lamentation for di princes of Israel,
and talk, ‘Wetin your mother be? Lioness! She lie down among lions. Among young lions she nourish her cubs.
She bring up one of her cubs. E become young lion. E learn to catch di prey. E devour men.
Di nations also hear of am. E dey taken for dem pit. Dem bring am with hooks to di land of Egypt.
Now when she see say she don wait, and her hope don perish, den she take another of her cubs, and make am young lion.
E go up and down among di lions. E become young lion. E learn to catch di prey. E devour men.
E know dem palaces, and lay waste dem cities. Di land dey desolate, and all wey dey inside am, because of di noise of im roaring.
Den di nations set against am on every side from di provinces. Dem spread dem net over am. E dey taken for dem pit.
Dem put am for cage with hooks, and bring am to di king of Babylon. Dem bring am into strongholds, so that im voice no go dey heard any more on di mountains of Israel.
Your mother dey like vine for your blood, planted by di waters. E dey fruitful and full of branches because of many waters.
E get strong branches for di sceptres of rulers, and im stature dey exalted among di thick boughs. E dey seen in im height, with di multitude of im branches.
But e dey plucked up in fury. E dey cast down to di ground, and di east wind dry up im fruit. Im strong branches dey broken off and wither. Di fire devour dem.
Now e dey planted for di wilderness, for dry and thirsty ground.
Fire don go out of im branches, wey devour im fruit, so that e no get strong branch again, sceptre to rule.’ Dis na lamentation, and e go be for lamentation.”
